title: Bug: logrotate can't free/delete log files when /var/log is 100% utilization on corner case
author: yejianquan
body: ### Is it platform specific generic ### Importance or Severity Critical ### Description of the bug **Abstract** , in a corner case, the log partition(/var/log) is with 100% utilization, and the logrotate will never release space, and no new logs can be write . Conditions that need to be met: 1. /var/log partition is 100% utilized. 2. The utilizations are on origin log files(e.g. syslog, auth.log, swss.asic0.rec), and no atchived log files(e.g. syslog.1, syslog.2.gz, sairedis.asic0.rec.1) 3. The logrotate will never free/delete log files on this scenario If log partition is small, for example in the test test_logrotate_small_size , it modifies the log partition to 300M. On chassi device, there's possible that the log partition is full before the first rotation: ``` admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ sudo df -k /var/log Filesystem 1K-blocks Used Available Use% Mounted on /dev/loop2 277623 259438 0 100% /var/log admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ ls -al /var/log total 12388 drwxr-xr-x 5 root root 1024 Jun 22 11:05 . drwxr-xr-x 1 root root 4096 Jun 20 13:00 .. -rw-r----- 1 root adm 53214 Jun 22 11:09 auth.log -rw-r----- 1 root adm 129 Jun 22 11:05 cron.log drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 1024 Jun 22 11:03 frr -rw-r----- 1 root adm 6288 Jun 22 11:07 gnmi.log -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jun 22 11:03 inventory.log drwxrwxrwx 2 root root 1024 Jun 22 11:04 ntpsec -rw-r----- 1 root adm 1866175 Jun 22 11:07 sai.log drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 1024 Jun 22 11:04 swss -rw-r----- 1 root adm 5228012 Jun 22 11:09 syslog -rw-r----- 1 root adm 5508441 Jun 22 11:05 teamd.log -rw-r----- 1 root adm 6496 Jun 22 11:07 telemetry.log admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ ls -al /var/log/swss total 258658 drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 1024 Jun 22 11:04 . drwxr-xr-x 5 root root 1024 Jun 22 11:05 .. -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 14946304 Jun 22 11:09 sairedis.asic0.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 15028224 Jun 22 11:09 sairedis.asic1.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 20819968 Jun 22 11:09 sairedis.asic2.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jun 22 11:04 sairedis.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 67215360 Jun 22 11:09 swss.asic0.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 69126602 Jun 22 11:09 swss.asic1.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 77720276 Jun 22 11:09 swss.asic2.rec admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ ``` There's no any archived log files (e.g. syslog.1, syslog.2.gz, sairedis.asic0.rec.1) , just the original log files (e.g. syslog, swss.asic0.rec) and it's full. When the logrotate is run, https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/abb529c331389fc05973cce8ef1f35f9e45facf4/files/image_config/logrotate/rsyslog.j2#L91 logrotate only seach of archived log files (e.g. syslog.1, syslog.2.gz, sairedis.asic0.rec.1), but there's not. ``` admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ find /var/log -type f -printf '%T+ %p\n' | grep -E '.+\.[0-9]+(\.gz)?$' | sort | awk 'NR == 1 {print $2}' admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ ``` So it skips, without any deletion of files, key log: **'No archive file to delete'** ``` admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ sudo /usr/sbin/logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.conf + NUM_LOGS_TO_ROTATE=8 + LOG_FILE_ROTATE_SIZE_KB=2048 + RESERVED_SPACE_KB=4096 + VAR_LOG_SIZE_KB=277623 + USABLE_SPACE_KB=245764 + THRESHOLD_KB=212996 + find /var/log/ -name *.1.gz -type f -exec rm -f {} + + true + du -s /var/log + awk { print $1; } + USED_KB=273526 + [ 273526 -lt 212996 ] + find /var/log -type f -printf %T+ %p\n + grep -E .+\.[0-9]+(\.gz)?$ + sort + awk NR == 1 {print $2} + OLDEST_ARCHIVE_FILE= + [ -z ] + logger -p syslog.err -t logrotate No archive file to delete -- potential for filling up /var/log partition! + break /usr/bin/mv: cannot stat '/var/log/sdk-init.log.3.gz': No such file or directory /usr/bin/mv: cannot stat '/var/log/sdk-init.log.2.gz': No such file or directory /usr/bin/mv: cannot stat '/var/log/sdk-init.log.1.gz': No such file or directory /usr/bin/mv: cannot stat '/var/log/sdk-init.log.gz': No such file or directory /usr/bin/cp: cannot stat '/var/log/sdk.log.1': No such file or directory gzip: /var/log/sdk-init.log: No such file or directory admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ ``` and it do rotation to convert them to .1 files: ``` admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ sudo df -k /var/log Filesystem 1K-blocks Used Available Use% Mounted on /dev/loop2 277623 273527 0 100% /var/log admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ ls -al /var/log total 12388 drwxr-xr-x 5 root root 1024 Jun 22 11:27 . drwxr-xr-x 1 root root 4096 Jun 20 13:00 .. -rw-r----- 1 root adm 0 Jun 22 11:29 auth.log -rw-r----- 1 root adm 53248 Jun 22 11:27 auth.log.1 -rw-r----- 1 root adm 0 Jun 22 11:27 cron.log -rw-r----- 1 root adm 508 Jun 22 11:25 cron.log.1 drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 1024 Jun 22 11:27 frr -rw-r----- 1 root adm 0 Jun 22 11:27 gnmi.log -rw-r----- 1 root adm 6288 Jun 22 11:07 gnmi.log.1 -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jun 22 11:03 inventory.log drwxrwxrwx 2 root root 1024 Jun 22 11:04 ntpsec -rw-r----- 1 root adm 0 Jun 22 11:27 sai.log -rw-r----- 1 root adm 1866175 Jun 22 11:07 sai.log.1 drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 1024 Jun 22 11:27 swss -rw-r----- 1 root adm 0 Jun 22 11:29 syslog -rw-r----- 1 root adm 5228541 Jun 22 11:27 syslog.1 -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jun 22 11:20 sysstat -rw-r----- 1 root adm 0 Jun 22 11:27 teamd.log -rw-r----- 1 root adm 5508441 Jun 22 11:05 teamd.log.1 -rw-r----- 1 root adm 0 Jun 22 11:27 telemetry.log -rw-r----- 1 root adm 6496 Jun 22 11:07 telemetry.log.1 admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ ls -al /var/log/swss total 258658 drwxr-xr-x 2 root root 1024 Jun 22 11:27 . drwxr-xr-x 5 root root 1024 Jun 22 11:27 .. -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jun 22 11:27 sairedis.asic0.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 14946304 Jun 22 11:27 sairedis.asic0.rec.1 -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jun 22 11:27 sairedis.asic1.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 15028224 Jun 22 11:27 sairedis.asic1.rec.1 -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jun 22 11:27 sairedis.asic2.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 20819968 Jun 22 11:27 sairedis.asic2.rec.1 -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jun 22 11:04 sairedis.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jun 22 11:27 swss.asic0.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 67215360 Jun 22 11:09 swss.asic0.rec.1 -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jun 22 11:27 swss.asic1.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 69126602 Jun 22 11:09 swss.asic1.rec.1 -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Jun 22 11:29 swss.asic2.rec -rw-r--r-- 1 root root 77720303 Jun 22 11:29 swss.asic2.rec.1 admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ ``` And the very trick thing happens, https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/abb529c331389fc05973cce8ef1f35f9e45facf4/files/image_config/logrotate/rsyslog.j2#L28-L39 The deletion of files only got triggered on the original files(e.g. syslog, auth.log, swss.asic0.rec). Because of the rotation, all of them are empty, and **since the partition is full, they're not writable, so they keeps empty**. **Logrotate will skip the deletion because they're empty files**, key logs: **"log does not need rotating (log is empty)"** ``` admin@str3-x-lc2-1:~$ sudo /usr/sbin/logrotate -vf /etc/logrotate.conf reading config file /etc/logrotate.conf including /etc/logrotate.d ``` ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Disable auto logrotate: ``` systemctl stop logrotate.timer ``` 2. Simulate small partition:sudo systemctl stop logrotate.timersudo fallocate -l 300M log-new-partition ``` sudo losetup -P /dev/loop2 log-new-partition sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/loop2 sudo mount /dev/loop2 /var/log ``` 2. Config reload to generate huge log files ``` config reload -y ``` 3. logrotate and can't rotate files: ``` sudo /usr/sbin/logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.conf ``` ### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior Actual: log files are not rotated/deleted Expected: log files should be rotated/deleted ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport` ```shell ``` ### Attach files (if any) _No response_

#### Why I did it
To fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/23053 ,

In a corner case, the log partition(/var/log) is with 100% utilization, and the logrotate will never release space, and no new logs can be write .
Conditions that need to be met:

1. /var/log partition is 100% utilized.
2. The utilizations are on origin log files(e.g. syslog, auth.log, swss.asic0.rec), and no atchived log files(e.g. syslog.1, syslog.2.gz, sairedis.asic0.rec.1)
3. The logrotate will never free/delete log files on this scenario

Add archived file clean up on log rotation, to make sure the log files can be rotated and deleted.
The logic will only be triggered on syslog(moved to the last one in the log list) rotation, to avoid useless scanning.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**: 33258706

#### How I did it
Add archived file clean up on log rotation, to make sure the log files can be rotated and deleted.
The logic will only be triggered on syslog rotation, to avoid useless scanning.
#### How to verify it
Verified:
1. Logrotate can deleted archived files when disk is full.
2. Logrotate works well on normal state.
